summary: On paper Pittsburgh has the edge (Pittsburgh ranks 2nd in broken tackles per touch, 6.2%), while Cleveland's best counter is to make them throw (Cleveland's defense ranks 12th in EPA per dropback, +0.05 allowed). Under center, Deshaun Watson ranks 20th of 30 in EPA per dropback and Aaron Rodgers ranks 27th; x-factor: Jaylen Warren gains +1.5 rushing yards over expected per carry, 2nd of 30, and Cleveland's run defense ranks 11th. The model favors Pittsburgh at 61%, mostly on rushing matchup (3.9 pts) and home field (1.6 pts).
